statement: Human pluripotent-stem-cell-derived cardiomyocytes grafted into infarcted non-human primate hearts formed substantial, host-synchronised new myocardium and improved contractile function — and caused ventricular arrhythmias in the treated animals.

measurement.endpoint: graft muscle, electromechanical coupling, contractile function, arrhythmia
measurement.effect: extensive remuscularisation and improved function; non-fatal ventricular arrhythmias in treated animals

evidence.note: pig heart; the same arrhythmia signal

replication.note: Three reports from overlapping Seattle groups (Murry, Laflamme). The arrhythmia finding reproduces across species within that programme; independent replication is what is missing.

drift: 'Stem cells regenerate the primate heart' — they do, and the recipients develop ventricular arrhythmia. The second half is rarely carried with the first.
limitations: short follow-up relative to a human therapy

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
